(def partition
  "Returns a lazy sequence of lists of n items each, at offsets step
  apart. If step is not supplied, defaults to n, i.e. the partitions
  do not overlap. If a pad collection is supplied, use its elements as
  necessary to complete last partition up to n items. In case there are
  not enough padding elements, return a partition with less than n items."
  (fn
    ([n coll]
     (partition n n coll))
    ([n step coll]
     (new LazySeq nil (fn* []
      (let [s (seq coll)]
        (when s
          (let [p (doall (take n s))]
            (when (= n (count p))
              (cons p (partition n step (drop step s)))))))) nil nil))
    ([n step pad coll]
     (new LazySeq nil (fn* []
      (let [s (seq coll)]
        (when s
          (let [p (doall (take n s))]
            (if (= n (count p))
              (cons p (partition n step pad (drop step s)))
              (list (take n (concat p pad)))))))) nil nil))))
rationale: Expand the complete pinned defn to def/fn, retaining its documentation (#30). lazy-seq is written as its expansion, a LazySeq of a thunk, since core is compiled before the macro. Follows Clojure: each partition is realized with doall and compared with =, not ==. Clojure steps with nthrest, which Suss lacks; drop yields the same elements lazily.
